projects.flagshipProject: Book of Record + Financial Activity Model + Financial Calculation Platform
projects.description: Wealthsimple's Book of Record is the authoritative record of client money and assets across the Trade, Cash, Managed Investing and Tax products: every trade, deposit, transfer, dividend, fee and settlement becomes a balanced accounting entry, and everything a client sees about their money is derived from it. A client moves money or places a trade in the app; the intent enters through the Financial Activity Model, the single validated and idempotent write funnel for financial intent, is committed to the ledger as balanced debit and credit entries, and is consumed by the Financial Calculation Platform and materialized read models that recompute balances, positions, book value and returns behind app balances, the activity feed, statements and tax slips. The estate is microservices on AWS with Apache Kafka as the event backbone, Kotlin, Python and Node.js services, a JSON-defined workflow engine driving long-running money movement, and a legacy Ruby on Rails monolith being decomposed behind anti-corruption layers; a Flow-to-TypeScript migration covered hundreds of thousands of lines across dozens of repositories. When a transfer, trade or account activity looks unusual, machine-learning models scored on the same activity and behavioral history flag it for review, classify reconciliation breaks and surface risk to operations teams, who release or correct it; those models ship on Wealthsimple's Machine Learning Platform, which takes a model from training to production in minutes rather than weeks, and an NVIDIA-backed AI Inference Platform serving dozens of production models at hundreds of millions of predictions a year, while an internal LLM Gateway gives hundreds of engineers a day secure redacted access to external model providers and powers AI-assisted migration of legacy financial logic into the Financial Activity Model. It touches the frontend layer (app balances, activity feeds, statements and internal operations tooling), the backend layer (Kafka-driven services, validation and posting pipelines, APIs and workflow orchestration), the data/AI layer (streaming calculation, materialized read models, feature extraction from ledger events, anomaly detection and model evaluation), the infrastructure layer (AWS, containers, GPU-backed inference, CI/CD and observability), and the security/governance layer (data redaction, access controls, auditability and regulated financial controls).
projects.notes: Publicly documented by Wealthsimple: Book of Record / Financial Activity Model / ledger / Financial Calculation Platform (engineering.wealthsimple.com/inside-the-book-of-record); Machine Learning Platform with sub-15-minute model deployment; NVIDIA-backed AI Inference Platform, 30+ models and 247M predictions in 12 months; LLM Gateway, 72,000+ requests at launch and ~500 daily users; Flow-to-TypeScript migration of 700,000+ lines across 40+ repos; Kafka event backbone, Ruby on Rails monolith decomposition, Java/Kotlin/Node.js/Python services and a JSON-defined workflow engine (engineering.wealthsimple.com, medium.com/wealthsimple). All figures are COMPANY/PLATFORM figures describing the project universe, NOT the candidate's personal attribution. Suncore, then operating as Sunroc Corporation, was modernizing the software and data workflows supporting its construction and materials businesses across the Intermountain West. The initiative connected customer and sales workflows with estimating, quoting, project and job-cost information, dispatch and fleet telemetry, materials operations, billing, and enterprise reporting so field and office teams could work from one consistent view of operational data instead of systems that had grown up separately. Cloud-based customer and operational platforms brought mobile access to crews and sales staff, while construction ERP capabilities carried project management, cost control, procurement and financial workflows. The hard problems were integrating field systems with corporate platforms, keeping job-cost and billing data reconcilable across sources, and making operational data trustworthy enough for teams to quote and dispatch from. It spans enterprise applications, backend integrations and APIs, operational and financial data pipelines, mobile and web workflows, reporting, reliability and security.
bullets: Built backend services and integrations that connected the cloud CRM used by sales and estimating with dispatch, telematics and job-cost systems, replacing manual re-keying between platforms that had grown up separately.

Delivered quoting and project workflows for ready-mix and construction operations, surfacing customer history and live operational data together so sales teams could price and commit work without leaving the application.
Developed data pipelines consolidating project, job-cost, materials and fleet telemetry into reporting models that gave operations and finance one reconcilable view across business units.
Built mobile-accessible field workflows and the APIs behind them so crews and dispatchers could record and retrieve operational data on site rather than routing everything through the office.
projects.notes: Company was Sunroc Corporation during this period; rebranded to Suncore Construction & Materials in 2025. Anchor is grounded in publicly reported Clyde Companies / Sunroc modernization (cloud CRM tailored to ready-mix, dispatch and telematics integration, mobile access) plus secondary reporting of a construction ERP implementation in 2018. projects.description: CIBC expanded its digital banking platform through this period from traditional online banking into a major mobile financial-services channel, launching Canada's first mobile banking application from a major bank in 2010 and then extending it across additional devices, brokerage, mobile web, tablet banking, payments and mobile cheque deposit. Clients could view accounts, transfer funds, pay bills, move money between people, access investing, and increasingly complete banking end to end from a phone. Supporting that required integration between client applications and core banking services, transaction and payment workflows, account and balance data, authentication and authorization, fraud and security controls, and the shared digital-channel services behind every banking experience. The hard problems were availability and correctness on money movement, securing a channel that was new to the bank, and evolving customer-facing applications on top of core systems that could not move at the same pace.
bullets: Built client-facing banking applications and the digital-channel services behind them as CIBC extended from online banking into mobile, covering account access, transfers, bill payment and person-to-person money movement.

Developed integration layers between customer applications and core banking systems, isolating channel development from mainframe release cycles so new digital-channel features could evolve without waiting on core-system release cycles.
Implemented authentication, authorization and transaction security controls for a channel that was new to the bank, working within the audit and regulatory requirements of Canadian retail banking.
Delivered payment and transaction workflows with the availability and correctness guarantees money movement demands, including reconciliation and failure handling on client-initiated transfers.
projects.notes: Anchor grounded in CIBC's publicly documented digital-channel history: first Canadian major-bank iPhone app (2010), BlackBerry and additional devices (2010), mobile brokerage (2011), mobile-optimized web and iPad banking (2012), mobile cheque deposit (2013).
